15.2 Descriptors
15.3 Enums
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/enums.py
from enum import Enum, auto, IntEnum, Flag

class Status(Enum):
    PENDING = auto()
    ACTIVE = auto()
    INACTIVE = auto()
    
    @classmethod
    def from_string(cls, value: str) -> "Status":
        return cls[value.upper()]

class Permission(Flag):
    READ = auto()
    WRITE = auto()
    EXECUTE = auto()
    ADMIN = READ | WRITE | EXECUTE

perm = Permission.READ | Permission.WRITE
print(Permission.WRITE in perm)  # True
```

sections.title: 15.4 Typing & Protocols
15.5 Networking & HTTP
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/networking.py
import requests
import httpx
import asyncio

# --- Requests (synchronous) ---
response = requests.get("https://api.github.com/users/octocat", timeout=10)
response.raise_for_status()
data = response.json()

# POST with JSON
response = requests.post(
    "https://api.example.com/users",
    json={"name": "Veera"},
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer token123"},
    timeout=10,
)

# Session (connection reuse)
with requests.Session() as session:
    session.headers.update({"Authorization": "Bearer token"})
    r1 = session.get("https://api.example.com/data1")
    r2 = session.get("https://api.example.com/data2")

# --- HTTPX (async-capable, modern) ---
async def fetch_multiple():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        tasks = [
            client.get(f"https://api.example.com/item/{i}")
            for i in range(10)
        ]
        responses = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        return [r.json() for r in responses]
```

sections.title: 15.6 Database Access
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/database.py
# --- SQLAlchemy (ORM) ---
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, Session, sessionmaker

Base = declarative_base()

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String(50), nullable=False)
    email = Column(String(100), unique=True)

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///app.db")
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

# CRUD
with SessionLocal() as session:
    user = User(name="Veera", email="veera@test.com")
    session.add(user)
    session.commit()
    
    users = session.query(User).filter(User.name == "Veera").all()
```

sections.title: 15.8 Comprehensions & Functional Programming
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/functional.py
from functools import reduce, partial, lru_cache
from operator import add, mul

# --- All Comprehension Types ---
list_comp   = [x**2 for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]
dict_comp   = {k: v for k, v in zip("abc", [1, 2, 3])}
set_comp    = {len(w) for w in ["hi", "hello", "hey"]}
gen_expr    = (x**2 for x in range(10))  # Generator expression

# --- Partial Functions ---
double = partial(mul, 2)
print(double(5))  # 10

# --- Reduce ---
total = reduce(add, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])  # 15

# --- Function composition ---
def compose(*funcs):
    def inner(x):
        for f in reversed(funcs):
            x = f(x)
        return x
    return inner

process = compose(str.upper, str.strip, lambda s: s.replace("  ", " "))
print(process("  hello   world  "))
```

sections.title: 15.9 Regular Expressions (Complete)
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/regex_complete.py
import re

# --- Common Patterns ---
patterns = {
    "email":    r"^[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w{2,}$",
    "phone":    r"^\+?\d{10,15}$",
    "url":      r"https?://[\w.-]+(?:/[\w.-]*)*",
    "ip_v4":    r"^(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$",
    "date":     r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$",
    "password": r"^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&]).{8,}$",
}

# --- Key Functions ---
re.match(r"\d+", "123abc")      # Match at START only
re.search(r"\d+", "abc123")     # Search anywhere
re.findall(r"\d+", "a1b2c3")   # All matches: ['1', '2', '3']
re.sub(r"\d+", "X", "a1b2c3")  # Replace: 'aXbXcX'
re.split(r"[,;]", "a,b;c")     # Split: ['a', 'b', 'c']

# --- Groups ---
m = re.search(r"(\w+)@(\w+)\.(\w+)", "user@domain.com")
print(m.group(0))   # user@domain.com (full match)
print(m.group(1))   # user
print(m.groups())    # ('user', 'domain', 'com')

# --- Named Groups ---
m = re.search(r"(?P<name>\w+):(?P<value>\d+)", "score:100")
print(m.group("name"))    # score
print(m.groupdict())      # {'name': 'score', 'value': '100'}

# --- Compiled Pattern (for repeated use) ---
pattern = re.compile(r"\b\w{4}\b")  # Exactly 4-letter words
words = pattern.findall("The quick brown fox jumps over lazy dogs")
```

sections.title: 15.10 Date & Time
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/datetime_module.py
from datetime import datetime, date, time, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo  # Python 3.9+

# --- Current time ---
now = datetime.now()
utc_now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
ist_now = datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata"))

# --- Formatting ---
formatted = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
parsed = datetime.strptime("2026-04-19", "%Y-%m-%d")

# --- Arithmetic ---
tomorrow = now + timedelta(days=1)
diff = datetime(2026, 12, 31) - now
print(diff.days)

# --- ISO format ---
iso_str = now.isoformat()
from_iso = datetime.fromisoformat(iso_str)
```

sections.title: 15.11 Weak References & Memory
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/memory.py
import sys
import weakref
import gc

# --- Reference counting ---
a = [1, 2, 3]
print(sys.getrefcount(a))  # 2 (a + getrefcount arg)

# --- Weak references (don't prevent garbage collection) ---
class Cache:
    def __init__(self):
        self._cache = weakref.WeakValueDictionary()
    
    def get(self, key):
        return self._cache.get(key)
    
    def set(self, key, value):
        self._cache[key] = value

# --- Memory profiling ---
# pip install memory_profiler
# @profile
# def my_func(): ...
# python -m memory_profiler script.py

# --- __slots__ for memory optimization ---
class Point:
    __slots__ = ('x', 'y')
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x, self.y = x, y
# Uses ~40% less memory than regular class with __dict__
```

## 📋 MASTER INTERVIEW Q&A CHEAT SHEET

Here are the **most commonly asked** questions across all topics:

| # | Question | One-Line Answer |
|---|----------|----------------|
| 1 | Mutable vs Immutable | Mutable can change in-place (list, dict), Immutable cannot (str, tuple, int) |
| 2 | `is` vs `==` | `is` checks identity (same object), `==` checks equality (same value) |
| 3 | `*args` vs `**kwargs` | `*args` = tuple of positional args, `**kwargs` = dict of keyword args |
| 4 | Class vs Object | Class = blueprint, Object = instance of that blueprint |
| 5 | Class vs Function | Class = data + behavior together, Function = single action |
| 6 | Decorator | Function that wraps another function to add behavior |
| 7 | Generator vs List | Generator yields lazily (memory efficient), List stores all in memory |
| 8 | GIL | Lock allowing only 1 thread to execute Python bytecode at a time |
| 9 | `@property` | Method accessed like attribute, adds getter/setter logic |
| 10 | `@classmethod` vs `@staticmethod` | classmethod gets `cls`, staticmethod gets nothing |
| 11 | SOLID | SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP — 5 design principles |
| 12 | Abstract class | Can't instantiate, forces subclasses to implement methods |
| 13 | Context manager | `__enter__`/`__exit__` — guarantees cleanup with `with` |
| 14 | Closure | Inner function remembering enclosing scope variables |
| 15 | Duck typing | Check behavior not type — "if it quacks like a duck..." |

## 🎯 INTERVIEW TIPS — How to Explain Any Topic Clearly

sections.title: The STAR-C Method for Technical Answers
sections.body:
1. **S**tatement — One-line definition
2. **T**echnical detail — How it works internally
3. **A**nalogy — Real-world comparison
4. **R**eal code — Quick example
5. **C**omparison — How it differs from similar concepts

sections.title: Example: "What is a decorator?"
sections.body:
> **Statement**: "A decorator is a function that takes another function and extends its behavior without modifying it."
> 
> **Technical**: "It works by wrapping the original function inside a new function. The `@decorator` syntax is syntactic sugar for `func = decorator(func)`."
> 
> **Analogy**: "Think of gift wrapping — the gift stays the same, but the wrapping adds presentation."
> 
> **Real code**: "`@timer` decorator that measures execution time — it calls `time.perf_counter()` before and after."
> 
> **Comparison**: "Unlike inheritance which adds behavior to classes, decorators add behavior to individual functions."
